newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close sharply higher on rising yen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close sharply higher on rising yen.

text.p: Stocks rose to a six-month closing high on hopes the Japanese yen's rises against the dollar could help boost South Korean exports, brokers said on Tuesday.
The composite index closed up 1.87 percent, or 13.47 points, to a provisional close of 734.67. It was the highest level since November 28 when it closed at 736.92.

The Japanese yen rose to as high as 112.80 yen per dollar in late Tuesday trading in Tokyo. A stronger yen would make South Korean products more competitive in world markets, where the two countries are major rivals for almost everything.
"The yen's strength came when investors began feeling relieved from the longstanding political and financial scandals," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities.
He said the market was escaping from the initial shock from the scandals with the arrests of President Kim Young-sam's second son on Saturday and one of his close associates on Monday.

Kim's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, was arrested for taking bribes and evading taxes. Kim Ki-sup, a former intelligence official, was put into a jail for taking kickbacks and peddling influence linked with a cable television broadcast licence.

Shipbuilders and other export-oriented manufacturers were among the main gainers. Daewoo Heavy Industries went limit up, gaining 560 won to its 1997 high of 7,660. Hanjin Heavy Industries rose 250 won to 9,150.
Despite the overall market's rally, the two listed units of the debt-ridden Dainong Group fell. The group was tapped on Monday to be bailed out from a financial crisis.
Midopa Department Store fell 650 won to its daily limit of 7,490 and Dainong Corp was down 250 won to its daily limit of 2,930.
The group's main creditor SEOULBANK said on Monday it would bail out the four companies by keeping their credit lines open even after they default on debt repayments.
SEOULBANK was unmoved by the troubles and gained 110 won to close at 3,700 won.
Falling interest rates driven by an ample cash liquidity were also seen as one of major factors to boost the buying sentiment.
The benchmark three-year corporate bond yields closed at 12.15 percent on Monday, down from as high as 12.33 percent a week before.
Index futures June contracts rose 0.10 points to 75.10 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index gained 1.64 points to 74.60.
